paragraphs: Differential privacy accounting tracks how privacy leakage accumulates when multiple private computations are combined. A central difficulty is that estimating a privacy parameter can be much easier than proving a strict upper bound on it. This paper introduces estimate-verify-release, or EVR, to connect those two tasks: an estimate becomes a proposed guarantee that must be checked before the query output is released.

The key component is a randomized verifier built using Monte Carlo techniques. Rather than treating a numerical estimate as sufficient evidence of privacy, EVR makes verification part of the release procedure. The authors also develop a Monte Carlo privacy accountant and report advantages in both accuracy and efficiency over existing accounting approaches.

The verifier and accountant apply to a commonly used class of differentially private algorithms that includes DP-SGD. An empirical evaluation finds that EVR improves the balance between privacy protection and machine-learning utility. The contribution therefore combines a formal approach to validating estimated guarantees with evidence that this approach can make private learning more useful.
neurips-2023-a-randomized-approach-to-ti.tldr: EVR uses randomized verification to turn estimated privacy parameters into formal guarantees and improve the utility–privacy tradeoff.

paragraphs: VICReg is a self-supervised learning method with promising results, but explaining why its objective produces useful representations remains a separate challenge. This paper studies that question through information theory. Its starting point is to derive information-theoretic quantities for deterministic networks, avoiding the stochastic-network assumptions that the authors regard as unrealistic.

The analysis connects optimization of the VICReg objective with optimization of mutual information, a quantity describing how much information variables share. The connection makes underlying assumptions explicit and provides a basis for comparing VICReg with other self-supervised methods. The authors also derive a generalization bound, linking the theoretical account to the usefulness of learned representations for downstream tasks.

The paper then uses the analysis to construct a family of self-supervised learning methods grounded in information-theoretic principles. These methods are reported to outperform existing techniques. The contribution is therefore both explanatory and constructive: it offers an account of VICReg’s behavior and uses that account to guide new objectives, rather than stopping at a theoretical interpretation.
neurips-2023-an-information-theory-persp.tldr: An information-theoretic analysis explains VICReg’s objective, establishes a generalization bound, and motivates improved self-supervised methods.

paragraphs: Segmenting a point cloud becomes difficult when different parts of an object or scene move independently. Identifying a part and understanding its transformation depend on each other: the model needs part assignments to describe separate motions, yet those motions affect the evidence used for assignment. Banana addresses this coupled problem through a network designed for inter-part equivariance.

The method repeatedly updates point-to-part assignments together with per-part SE(3)-equivariance, which concerns rotations and translations in three dimensions. These updates solve a fixed-point problem, seeking a state that remains unchanged under further iteration. The authors derive both equivariance at each step and global convergence, yielding an equivariant final state.

This formulation gives a precise treatment of how segmentation should respond to transformations of individual parts. Experiments on articulated objects and scans containing multiple objects show strong generalization to inter-part transformations, including substantial changes in point-cloud geometry and topology. The findings support jointly evolving the assignments and transformation behavior as a way to handle previously unseen arrangements of parts.
neurips-2023-banana-banach-fixed-point-n.tldr: Banana jointly refines part assignments and transformation behavior to produce convergent, inter-part-equivariant point-cloud segmentation.

paragraphs: Two recurrent neural networks can implement equivalent computations even when the geometric arrangements of their internal states differ. Comparisons based only on those arrangements can therefore miss a shared computational process. This paper introduces Dynamical Similarity Analysis, or DSA, to compare how neural activity evolves over time, shifting the comparison toward the dynamics that carry out recurrent computation.

DSA first learns a high-dimensional linear system that captures core features of the original nonlinear dynamics. It then compares the embedded systems using an extension of Procrustes Analysis. This comparison accounts for how vector fields, which describe the direction of state evolution, change under orthogonal transformations.

Across four case studies, DSA distinguishes recurrent networks with conjugate dynamics from those without that relationship, where geometric methods fall short. The authors also show that it can distinguish learning rules without supervision. These results support using temporal structure to investigate whether networks share internal processes, with relevance to comparisons across artificial networks and neural circuits.
neurips-2023-beyond-geometry-comparing-t.tldr: DSA compares neural systems through their temporal dynamics, revealing relationships that comparisons of state geometry can miss.

paragraphs: Counterfactual fairness asks whether a person’s classification would stay the same if their protected class were different. That question is intuitive, but its counterfactual comparison cannot be directly observed. Group fairness measures are easier to calculate from data. This paper investigates when the causal structure behind the data connects these two kinds of fairness.

The authors first show that fairness and accuracy need not fundamentally conflict: under plausible conditions, a counterfactually fair predictor is accuracy-optimal in an unbiased target distribution. They then develop a correspondence between the data-generating causal graph and the group fairness measures, if any, that are equivalent to counterfactual fairness.

In the three contexts studied, measurement error connects counterfactual fairness to demographic parity, selection on labels connects it to equalized odds, and selection on predictors connects it to calibration. These are context-dependent equivalences, rather than interchangeable fairness rules. The practical implication is that counterfactual fairness can sometimes be assessed through relatively simple observable group measures when the relevant causal context supports that connection.
neurips-2023-causal-context-connects-cou.tldr: Causal context determines when observable group fairness measures capture counterfactual fairness and when fair prediction can also be accuracy-optimal.

paragraphs: Probabilistic circuits represent complex distributions by combining simpler distributions in ways that keep reasoning computationally manageable. However, learning them becomes challenging when data contain heterogeneous types, and some useful distributions lack a closed-form density. Characteristic circuits address these issues by changing the mathematical representation used to describe the distributions.

The proposed models operate in the spectral domain through characteristic functions. Because a characteristic function uniquely corresponds to a probability measure, this representation can describe a distribution even when a convenient density formula is unavailable. The paper uses that relationship to provide a unified treatment of high-dimensional heterogeneous data while supporting efficient probabilistic inference.

The authors show that both the structure and parameters of characteristic circuits can be learned efficiently from data. On common benchmark datasets involving heterogeneous domains, the models outperform state-of-the-art density estimators. The significance is that tractable uncertainty modeling need not depend on every component distribution having an explicit density: a different representation can preserve useful inference and learning capabilities.
neurips-2023-characteristic-circuits-6ca.tldr: Characteristic circuits use characteristic functions to learn tractable distributions over heterogeneous data, including cases without closed-form densities.

paragraphs: Language-model pretraining depends on choosing text that fits the intended target distribution. This paper formulates selection as finding a subset of a large unlabeled collection that matches unlabeled target examples. Its method, Data Selection with Importance Resampling, or DSIR, adapts importance resampling to make that matching practical at the scale of language-model datasets.

DSIR estimates importance weights in a reduced feature space, then uses those weights to sample documents. An implementation based on hashed n-gram features selects 100 million documents from the full Pile in 4.5 hours. The authors also define KL reduction to measure how closely selected data approach the target in a chosen feature space.

Across eight selection methods, KL reduction using hashed n-grams correlates strongly with average downstream accuracy, with r=0.82. DSIR performs comparably to expert curation for continued pretraining across eight target distributions. For general-domain pretraining targeting Wikipedia and books, it improves GLUE performance by 2–2.5% over random selection and heuristic filtering. These findings support compact text statistics as useful guides for scalable data selection.
neurips-2023-data-selection-for-language.tldr: DSIR efficiently selects language-model training text by resampling documents according to how well their compact features match target data.

paragraphs: Planning in Minecraft requires sustained, precise reasoning across many steps. A plan can also be inefficient when it orders independent subgoals without considering what the current agent can achieve most readily. This paper introduces DEPS, short for Describe, Explain, Plan and Select, to address both difficulties through an interactive planning approach based on large language models.

DEPS uses feedback during execution to improve error correction over long tasks. It also includes a learned goal Selector that ranks parallel subgoals by their estimated number of steps to completion. This gives the planner a way to adjust the ordering of goals according to their estimated proximity for the agent.

The authors report a zero-shot multitask agent that robustly completes more than 70 Minecraft tasks and nearly doubles overall performance in their experiments. Further evaluations show effectiveness in ALFWorld and tabletop manipulation. Ablation and exploratory studies examine the design and progress on ObtainDiamond. Together, the findings support combining feedback-driven plan revision with a learned estimate of which subgoals are more immediately achievable.
neurips-2023-describe-explain-plan-and-s.tldr: DEPS combines feedback-based LLM planning with learned subgoal ordering to improve agents’ performance on long, multistep tasks.

paragraphs: Answering questions about a video with several human-object interactions requires finding the events that matter to the question. Glance-Focus approaches this through event memories that guide later attention. The motivation is that a fixed vocabulary of detected actions may transfer poorly across video domains, so the model generates dynamic event memories instead.

During the glancing stage, an encoder-decoder produces a set of memories. The paper develops both a supervised method using bipartite matching and an unsupervised alternative that removes dependence on event annotations. During focusing, the question first guides attention toward a relevant event memory, then toward the corresponding video moment through multilevel cross-attention.

The memories therefore connect high-level event concepts in a question with detailed content spread across a long video. Experiments on STAR, EgoTaskQA, AGQA, and NExT-QA report state-of-the-art results, including improvements over current large models on challenging reasoning tasks. The findings support organizing video evidence around generated events to help the model locate the moments needed for an answer.
neurips-2023-glance-and-focus-memory-pro.tldr: Glance-Focus generates event memories that guide question-specific attention to relevant moments in videos containing multiple events.

paragraphs: Distributed learning systems may need to be fair and robust at the same time, yet satisfying both properties creates difficulties that studying either alone can miss. This paper identifies differences between participants’ datasets as a key obstacle. It asks why the goals are difficult to combine, whether their combination can be theoretically guaranteed, and how robustness mechanisms affect fairness.

The proposed framework, H-nobs, combines an objective designed to promote fairness with a robust aggregation method called norm-based screening. The authors explain why this screening method fits their framework compared with other robust aggregation approaches. The design thus addresses fairness through the learning objective and robustness through how contributions are aggregated.

The paper establishes convergence theorems for nonconvex, convex, and strongly convex learning models, providing theoretical guarantees for the two properties. It also empirically examines how norm-based screening influences fairness performance. This makes the interaction between fairness and robustness an explicit object of study, alongside the construction of a framework intended to provide both.
neurips-2023-h-nobs-achieving-certified-.tldr: H-nobs combines a fairness-promoting objective with norm-based screening and establishes fairness and robustness guarantees for distributed learning.

paragraphs: Molecular learning often has plentiful unlabeled data but few experimentally obtained labels. Self-supervised learning can help, although choosing useful views of a molecule is a central design problem. This paper studies persistent homology, a mathematical tool that describes topological features surviving across multiple scales, as a foundation for learning molecular representations.

Persistent homology offers multiple views of data, stability in preserving distances, and flexibility for incorporating domain knowledge. The authors investigate an autoencoder to assess its representational power and propose a contrastive loss that complements existing methods. These two components examine both what the topological representation can capture and how it can improve other self-supervised approaches.

Evaluations on molecular property prediction find more predictive representations across different probing tasks after self-supervised learning. Adding the proposed loss improves baseline performance, sometimes substantially, and the method often produces substantial gains on very small datasets. These qualified findings are especially relevant to molecular applications where obtaining labels is costly and the available supervised training set is limited.
neurips-2023-improving-self-supervised-m.tldr: Persistent homology supplies multiscale molecular representations and a complementary contrastive loss that improve property prediction, often on very small datasets.

paragraphs: Many modern architectures reuse the same weights across different parts of a computation. That shared structure complicates the application of K-FAC, a second-order optimization method intended to accelerate neural-network training. This paper develops a framework for linear layers with weight sharing, covering a common component of transformers, convolutional networks, and graph neural networks.

The authors identify two settings that motivate K-FAC-expand and K-FAC-reduce. Each variant is exact for deep linear networks with weight sharing in its corresponding setting. K-FAC-reduce is generally faster, and the paper uses that advantage to accelerate automatic hyperparameter selection through marginal-likelihood optimization for a Wide ResNet.

When training a graph neural network and a vision transformer, the two variants show little difference in performance. Both reach a fixed validation target using 50–75% as many steps as a first-order reference run, with comparable wall-clock improvements. These experiments support the practical potential of extending K-FAC to shared-weight architectures, while the exactness results apply specifically to the stated deep linear settings.
neurips-2023-kronecker-factored-approxim.tldr: Two K-FAC variants extend curvature-based optimization to weight-sharing layers and reduce training steps and time in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: A temporal sequence contains both particular items and an order relating those items. Experimental evidence suggests the brain represents these aspects separately, but the mechanism remains unclear. This paper investigates how a recurrent neural circuit can learn an abstract order representation and reuse it with different sequence contents.

With an appropriate learning protocol, the circuit learns tree-structured attractor states that encode the corresponding branching order of the training sequences. These states form a temporal template that can be bound to different contents. Separating the order template from its contents provides a way to reuse an existing organizational structure when processing another sequence.

In a transfer-learning task, reusing a template helps acquire new sequences with the same or similar order structure. In a keyword-spotting task, the attractor representation improves robustness when order is the key information distinguishing sequences. The findings demonstrate a possible computational mechanism for flexible sequence processing, with the robustness result explicitly tied to tasks where ordinal information matters.
neurips-2023-learning-and-processing-the.tldr: Recurrent circuits can learn reusable attractor templates for sequence order, aiding transfer and robustness when order distinguishes sequences.

paragraphs: Mixed integer linear programming solvers benefit from finding feasible solutions early because those solutions help guide branch-and-bound search. Diving heuristics pursue solutions by repeatedly modifying and resolving linear programs along a depth-first search. Existing divers use generic rules, which can overlook shared structure among similar problem instances.

L2Dive learns specialized diving heuristics with graph neural networks. It trains generative models to predict variable assignments, then uses linear-programming duality to translate those predictions into diving decisions. The method is fully integrated into SCIP, connecting learned predictions to an established optimization solver’s search procedure.

Across a range of combinatorial optimization problems, L2Dive finds better feasible solutions than standard divers. For server load balancing and neural-network verification, the reported average improvements in the primal-dual integral reach up to 7% against a tuned baseline and 35% against a default baseline. Average solving time falls by 20% and 29%, respectively. These results show that exploiting recurring problem structure can improve both solution discovery and overall solving performance.
neurips-2023-learning-to-dive-in-branch-.tldr: L2Dive uses graph-neural-network predictions to guide diving heuristics, improving feasible solutions and solving times in reported optimization tasks.

paragraphs: In partial label learning, each example comes with several candidate labels, exactly one of which is correct. The challenge is to resolve that ambiguity. This paper combines evidence about which examples are similar with evidence about which are semantically dissimilar, using their opposition to narrow the possible label-confidence assignments.

A constrained regression model first estimates confidence in the candidate labels. Multiplying the confidence matrix by its transpose produces global pairwise similarities. Separately, candidate-label intersections supply initial dissimilarity information, which is spread across the dataset using the local geometry of examples. The two matrices constrain each other, shrinking the solution space for label confidence while refining dissimilarity information.

The authors extend the model with a kernel formulation to capture nonlinear structure and solve it with an inexact augmented Lagrange multiplier method. They provide theoretical guarantees and report significant improvements over state-of-the-art partial-label methods on ten artificial and seven real-world datasets. The central contribution is to make dissimilarity an active source of label disambiguation alongside similarity.
neurips-2023-partial-label-learning-with.tldr: The method resolves ambiguous labels by jointly refining similarity and propagated dissimilarity to constrain candidate-label confidence.

paragraphs: When inputs lie on a curved geometric space, a Gaussian process can be built directly on that space or obtained by restricting a Euclidean process to it. This paper asks whether theoretical learning rates can establish an advantage for the intrinsic construction. It studies posterior contraction, describing how a posterior concentrates as observations accumulate.

The authors prove optimal contraction rates for intrinsic Matérn Gaussian processes on compact Riemannian manifolds. They also derive rates for extrinsic processes using mathematical connections between function spaces on the manifold and in the surrounding space. When the smoothness parameters are matched appropriately, the intrinsic and extrinsic rates coincide.

Empirical examples nevertheless show that intrinsic processes can perform better in practice, consistent with prior observations described in the abstract. Thus, matching contraction rates do not settle the question of practical data efficiency. The paper argues for finer analyses, particularly for small datasets and behavior before asymptotic rates become informative, to distinguish benefits that the shared rates do not capture.
neurips-2023-posterior-contraction-rates.tldr: Intrinsic and extrinsic Matérn Gaussian processes have matching contraction rates under appropriate smoothness matching, despite possible practical advantages for intrinsic models.

paragraphs: One view of reinforcement learning treats decision-making as probabilistic inference over a model of the environment. A central quantity is the probability that an optimal policy visits a particular state-action pair. This paper argues that earlier approximations to this quantity can be arbitrarily poor and develops a rigorous Bayesian treatment of state-action optimality.

The authors explain how the posterior probability propagates through the Markov decision process and show that it can generate an exploration policy with efficient regret behavior. Exact computation is intractable, so they introduce a variational Bayesian approximation. This approximation leads to a tractable convex optimization problem while retaining an efficient-exploration result for the resulting policy.

The approach, VAPOR, has strong connections to Thompson sampling, K-learning, and maximum-entropy exploration. Experiments with a deep reinforcement-learning version demonstrate a performance advantage. The contribution links a carefully defined Bayesian target to a practical approximation, providing theoretical support for exploration as well as empirical evidence for a neural implementation.
neurips-2023-probabilistic-inference-in-.tldr: VAPOR derives a tractable Bayesian approximation to state-action optimality with efficient-exploration guarantees and encouraging deep-RL results.

paragraphs: Synthetic tabular data can support machine learning when real data are scarce or inaccessible. However, matching broad statistical properties does not necessarily preserve the nuances that make a dataset useful. This paper examines how data-centric methods that profile the original data can guide generation toward more representative synthetic examples.

The authors investigate the consequences of ignoring these profiles even when generated data appear statistically faithful. They propose an evaluation framework for assessing the integration of data profiles into generation. An empirical study applies the framework to five state-of-the-art tabular generators across eleven datasets, examining both successes and limitations of current approaches.

The paper turns its findings into recommendations concerning classification performance, model selection, and feature selection. Its central implication is that synthetic-data quality should be assessed in relation to the structure and uses of the source data, alongside statistical fidelity. Profiling provides a way to bring those considerations into both the generation process and the evaluation of the resulting datasets.
neurips-2023-reimagining-synthetic-tabul.tldr: A benchmark of five tabular generators examines how data profiling can improve synthetic-data generation and evaluation beyond statistical fidelity.

paragraphs: Neural networks can overfit incorrect labels, so some training methods favor examples with small training losses as likely to be correctly labeled. For time series, recording noise can distort the patterns needed for classification. A correctly labeled example may consequently have a large loss, making that selection rule less dependable.

Scale-teaching uses multiple neural networks trained simultaneously on different temporal scales. A fine-to-coarse fusion mechanism helps them learn discriminative patterns, while cross-teaching uses complementary information across scales to choose small-loss examples as clean training data. The selection decision therefore draws on multiple views of the sequence rather than a single scale.

The method also attempts to recover useful information from unselected examples. It constructs multiscale embedding graphs and propagates labels from selected clean examples to correct the labels of large-loss examples. Experiments across multiple time-series benchmarks report better effectiveness and robustness than state-of-the-art methods. The approach joins cross-scale sample selection with label correction to address the combined difficulty of noisy recordings and noisy labels.
neurips-2023-scale-teaching-robust-multi.tldr: Scale-teaching combines cross-scale training, clean-sample selection, and graph-based label correction for time-series classification with noisy labels.

paragraphs: The Tanimoto coefficient measures similarity between molecules represented by discrete fingerprints and can serve as a kernel in machine learning. Random-feature approximations can make many kernel methods more scalable, but suitable approximations for the Tanimoto kernel have been lacking. This paper develops two kinds of random features to fill that gap.

The construction also yields a new extension of the kernel to real-valued vectors. The authors characterize the proposed features theoretically and bound the spectral-norm error of the Gram matrix, the matrix of pairwise kernel similarities. This gives an account of approximation error at the level of the similarity matrix used by kernel methods.

Experiments show that the random features approximate Tanimoto similarities effectively on real-world datasets and are useful for molecular property prediction and optimization. The contribution connects a familiar molecular similarity measure with a computational approach suited to larger datasets. It also broadens the representation beyond discrete fingerprints through the real-valued extension developed alongside the approximations.
neurips-2023-tanimoto-random-features-fo.tldr: Two random-feature constructions make Tanimoto kernel methods more scalable and introduce an extension to real-valued vectors.

paragraphs: Budget-feasible mechanisms aim to obtain valuable outcomes while respecting a spending limit and accounting for participants’ incentives. This paper revisits their design for submodular valuation functions, a setting relevant to crowdsourcing and social marketing. It introduces TripleEagle, a framework for constructing mechanisms that combine solution quality with computational and strategic simplicity.

The resulting mechanisms improve approximation ratios over the state of the art for both monotone and non-monotone submodular valuations. These ratios describe how closely a mechanism’s outcome can approximate the optimal value. Covering both cases addresses settings where adding more selected participants or items can only help, as well as settings where it need not.

The authors also report the first mechanisms in this literature that combine linear computational complexity with obvious strategyproofness. This pairs efficient computation with a strong incentive property intended to make truthful participation straightforward. Extensive experiments support the mechanisms’ efficiency and effectiveness. The contribution therefore addresses several requirements for practical use together, rather than measuring progress solely through approximation quality.
neurips-2023-triple-eagle-simple-fast-an.tldr: TripleEagle improves approximation guarantees for budget-feasible mechanisms while combining linear complexity with obvious strategyproofness.

paragraphs: When several people speak in a reverberant room, each microphone records a different mixture of their voices. UNSSOR uses recordings with more microphones than speakers to train speech separation without isolated speech targets. The key constraint is that the estimated contributions of all speakers at each microphone should sum to that microphone’s observed mixture.

At each training step, a neural network produces intermediate estimates for individual speakers. Linear filters then adapt those estimates to the microphone mixtures, and a loss measures whether the filtered signals reconstruct each recording. The filters are calculated separately in frequency sub-bands using forward convolutive prediction. An additional loss addresses inconsistent speaker assignments across frequencies by minimizing intra-source magnitude scattering.

The training procedure requires over-determined mixtures, but the resulting networks can perform under-determined separation, including separation from a single microphone. Evaluations on two-speaker mixtures in reverberant conditions demonstrate effectiveness and potential. The important distinction is that multiple training microphones supply constraints that can support a model intended for fewer microphones at use time.
neurips-2023-unssor-unsupervised-neural-.tldr: UNSSOR learns speech separation from multichannel mixture constraints and can train models for single-microphone separation.

paragraphs: A video contains repeated patterns and relationships between neighboring frames that can provide evidence for repairing corrupted content. This paper builds a video-enhancement framework around those internal statistics. It learns the weights of neural modules directly from the corrupted test sequence, without requiring an external collection of training videos.

The approach uses coherence across space and time, together with a spatial pyramid loss. That loss draws on the recurrence of video patches at different scales, bringing multiscale repetition into the optimization objective. The authors find that this improves robustness to unstructured noise affecting both spatial content and temporal behavior.

The framework covers denoising, object removal, frame interpolation, and super-resolution. Qualitative and quantitative evaluations use DAVIS, UCF-101, and VIMEO90K-T, with state-of-the-art results reported for denoising, object removal, and frame interpolation. These findings support learning from the particular video being processed: its repeated structure can supply a useful prior for enhancement even when the input frames themselves are degraded.
neurips-2023-video-dynamics-prior-an-int.tldr: Video Dynamics Prior learns directly from a corrupted video, using multiscale repetition and temporal coherence to support robust enhancement.

paragraphs: Diffusion models generate content through a learned process of reversing noise corruption. Prior studies have shown that basic unconditional models can contain backdoors: embedded input patterns that trigger manipulated outputs. VillanDiffusion expands the scope of this security analysis so that it covers more of the configurations used in diffusion-based generation.

The framework includes both unconditional and conditional models, spanning denoising-based and score-based approaches. It also covers multiple training-free samplers. Bringing these configurations into one framework enables broader evaluations of backdoor behavior across choices of model formulation, conditioning, and sampling, rather than limiting analysis to the basic unconditional settings previously studied.

Experiments show that the framework facilitates analysis across different diffusion-model configurations and yields new insights into caption-based backdoors. Caption-based analysis is particularly relevant to the conditional generation setting highlighted in the paper, including text-to-image applications. The stated contribution is a unified way to investigate these vulnerabilities across configurations, together with experimental evidence that the framework supports that broader investigation.
neurips-2023-villandiffusion-a-unified-b.tldr: VillanDiffusion unifies backdoor analysis across conditional and unconditional diffusion models, multiple formulations, and different samplers.

paragraphs: Offline safe reinforcement learning seeks policies that earn rewards while satisfying safety constraints using only previously collected data. This matters when further interaction would be costly or dangerous. A major challenge is evaluating actions poorly represented in that data: errors in estimating their rewards and safety costs can undermine policy optimization.

VOCE reformulates the problem as probabilistic inference and introduces variational distributions to make policy optimization more flexible. It then uses pessimistic estimates for both reward and cost Q-values, which summarize the consequences of taking actions. These conservative estimates are intended to reduce extrapolation errors associated with actions outside the dataset’s distribution.

Across multiple experimental tasks, VOCE achieves competitive performance and particularly strong safety results relative to state-of-the-art algorithms. The findings support combining flexible probabilistic optimization with conservative evaluation of unfamiliar actions. The safety improvement is an empirical result of the reported experiments, showing how this combination can help manage the tension between pursuing reward and respecting safety constraints in offline learning.
neurips-2023-voce-variational-optimizati.tldr: VOCE combines variational policy optimization with conservative reward and cost estimates to improve safety in offline reinforcement-learning experiments.
